question: Who started the first district nursing scheme in Liverpool to care for poor families right in their homes?

options.A: William Rathbone

question: A nurse receives a batch of donated nutrition teaching materials from an NGO. What is the best way to use them?

options.C: Throw them away because they did not come from the ministry

question: How is the relationship between the skin and underlying muscle described using directional terms?

question: What is the standard recommended temperature range for storing most routine vaccines in a cold chain?

options.D: Between +15°C and +25°C

question: How can nurses best help alleviate the mental stress of patients in quarantine?

options.A: By telling them that their fears are completely irrational

options.C: By restricting all telephone and internet access for safety reasons
options.D: By avoiding any conversation about why they are confined

explanation: Maintaining social connection and offering empathetic communication significantly reduces psychological distress. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T5#GNS313_U2_T5_h7)

question: What is the main job of the pneumotaxic center in the pons?

options.A: Controlling fine motor skills in the hands

options.C: Processing visual images from the retina
options.D: Regulating conscious thought processes

explanation: Think of the pneumotaxic center as a smooth rhythm controller for breathing, helping you switch easily between breathing in and breathing out. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T20#GNS211_U3_T20_h3)

question: Why should the fluid bag be kept at a low height during a washout?

options.D: To allow the nurse to check the temperature of the solution

question: How does a just culture handle a nurse who makes an honest, unintentional mistake?

options.A: By reporting them to the police for criminal negligence

options.C: By ignoring the incident entirely to protect team morale
options.D: By offering coaching, support, and looking at the system flaws that contributed

explanation: Honest mistakes are treated as learning opportunities involving system factors, rather than automatic grounds for harsh discipline. [learn more](GST319_U6_T1#GST319_U6_T1_h2)

question: Which tool does a nurse grab to take a look inside a patient's ear canal and ear drum?

options.A: An ophthalmoscope
options.B: A tongue depressor
options.C: A stethoscope
options.D: An otoscope

question: A patient complains of sudden vulval redness and intense itching after starting a new brand of scented bubble bath. What is the most likely cause?

options.B: A chronic autoimmune joint disorder
options.C: An irritant or allergic contact reaction
options.D: A congenital anatomical defect

explanation: Chemicals and fragrances in bubble baths often trigger contact dermatitis on the sensitive skin of the vulva. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T6#GNS216_U5_T6_h2)

question: If a student wants to study how hospital room ventilation and fresh air affect patient healing, which theory fits best?

options.A: Callista Roy’s Adaptation Model
options.B: Dorothea Orem’s Self-Care Deficit Theory
options.C: Florence Nightingale’s Environmental Theory
options.D: Madeleine Leininger’s Culture Care Theory

explanation: You nailed it! Nightingale was the pioneer of using clean air, light, and a healthy environment to help patients recover. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T12#GNS217_U3_T12_h4)

question: What happens when a nursing study uncovers surprising or unexpected findings?

options.A: The entire scientific community must stop investigating that topic
options.B: The study is immediately thrown away and hidden
options.C: Patients on the ward are taken off their medication
options.D: It opens the door for new research questions and follow-up studies

explanation: Spot on! Unexpected results are not failures; they challenge what we think we know and kick off the next round of helpful research. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T1#GNS217_U2_T1_h5)

question: Which of these is a great example of cost-effective healthcare planning?

options.A: Purchasing expensive imported machines instead of servicing local ones
options.B: Waiting until patients are critically ill before treating them
options.C: Focusing heavily on preventive health education in the community
options.D: Throwing away opened medication vials at the end of every shift

explanation: Brilliant! Stopping a disease before it starts is always much cheaper and easier than treating late-stage sickness. [learn more](GST322_U5_T5#GST322_U5_T5_h5)

question: What do we call a patient who keeps shedding germs even after they've started feeling better?

options.A: Incubation carrier
options.B: Susceptible host
options.C: Acute clinical case
options.D: Convalescent carrier

explanation: A convalescent carrier is someone who is recovering and feeling good again, but their body is still letting out a few leftover germs. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T5#GNS313_U1_T5_h3)

question: How did healthcare delivery change globally after Primary Health Care was introduced?

options.A: It focused exclusively on building high-tech specialist hospitals in rural areas
options.B: It transferred all health responsibilities away from governments to private individuals
options.C: It eliminated traditional medicine entirely in favor of imported pharmaceuticals
options.D: It shifted from expensive hospital-centric curative care to community-based preventive care

explanation: You got it! Before PHC, the system waited for people to fall sick and travel far to hospitals. PHC changed this by bringing prevention and basic care directly to the people. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T3#GNS124_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why is it usually a bad idea to react and make big changes over every single tiny up-and-down blip on a data chart?

options.A: It prevents nurses from taking their mandatory tea breaks
options.B: It violates government health privacy laws
options.C: It breaks hospital computer monitors and wastes paper
options.D: It leads to unnecessary tampering with normal system variation

explanation: Everyday systems naturally have minor ups and downs. Overreacting to normal bumps can actually mess up a workflow that is working just fine! [learn more](GST319_U3_T2#GST319_U3_T2_h5)

question: Which of these is a typical source of chemical waste in a hospital?

options.A: Leftover food trays from patient bedsides
options.B: Paper wrappers from sterile surgical gloves
options.C: Discarded lab reagents and cleaning solvents
options.D: Cotton wool balls soaked in sterile water

explanation: You'll find chemical waste coming from cleaning supplies, disinfectants, and laboratory testing chemicals. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h6)

question: Who are considered key stakeholders in community mental health mobilisation?

options.A: Only patients currently admitted to psychiatric wards
options.B: Foreign investors and international tourists
options.C: Traditional leaders, religious heads, and local groups
options.D: Only certified psychiatric doctors from abroad

explanation: Local leaders and grassroots groups hold the trust of the community and are vital partners for successful health campaigns. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T7#GNS314_U4_T7_h3)

question: If a patient takes a drug that blocks muscarinic receptors, what bodily response would you expect?

options.A: Increased digestion and bowel movement
options.B: Constriction of the pupils
options.C: Increased saliva production
options.D: Increased heart rate

explanation: Blocking these receptors turns off the calming parasympathetic brake on the heart, making it beat faster, while slowing down things like digestion. You are thinking like a real nurse! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T31#GNS211_U3_T31_h4)

question: What should you do when a patient's unique situation doesn't quite match standard textbook research?

options.A: Assume the research is completely useless and rely only on guesses
options.B: Use critical thinking to balance the evidence with the patient's individual reality
options.C: Discharge the patient immediately without further assessment
options.D: Ignore the patient's symptoms because the textbook study is always right

explanation: Research gives us a great roadmap, but every patient is unique. As a nurse, you use your critical thinking to adapt care to the person in front of you. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T3#GNS217_U1_T3_h8)

question: Why should nurse researchers use both traditional and modern ways to share their work?

options.A: To guarantee that the research costs no money to produce
options.B: To avoid having to write formal nursing reports ever again
options.C: To reach both academic scholars and active frontline workers
options.D: To make sure nobody ever reads the original study data

explanation: You're doing great! Different people look for information in different places, so mixing formats helps your message travel further. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T1#GNS224_U4_T1_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of community health care financing?

options.A: To eliminate all taxes paid by citizens
options.B: To raise, pool, and allocate funds for health services
options.C: To replace government budgets entirely
options.D: To generate profit for private hospital owners

explanation: Financing systems focus on gathering resources and distributing them effectively so health services remain available to the population. [learn more](GST322_U4_T4#GST322_U4_T4_h1)

question: How many links make up the traditional chain of infection?

options.A: Ten
options.B: Four
options.C: Six
options.D: Three

explanation: The chain of infection consists of six distinct links that must all be present for an infection to spread successfully. [learn more](GST114_U2_T17#GST114_U2_T17_h2)

question: Why do younger adolescents frequently abuse household inhalants like glue and solvents?

options.A: They are prescribed routinely by pediatricians
options.B: They are cheap and legally sold household items
options.C: They do not cause any harm to the brain
options.D: They have pleasant long-lasting medical benefits

explanation: Inhalants are popular among younger teens because they are inexpensive, accessible, and easily found in everyday household products. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T13#GNS312_U3_T13_h2)

question: Which blood pressure range is classified as Stage 1 Hypertension?

options.A: 140 or higher systolic or 90 or higher diastolic
options.B: Below 120 systolic and below 80 diastolic
options.C: 130-139 systolic or 80-89 diastolic
options.D: 120-129 systolic and under 80 diastolic

question: What major historical event drove Florence Nightingale to collect and analyze health data?

options.A: The American Civil War
options.B: The Crimean War
options.C: World War I
options.D: The 1918 Influenza Pandemic

explanation: Nightingale systematically tracked illness and death rates among wounded soldiers during her service in the Crimean War to prove the value of hospital sanitation. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T3#GNS217_U2_T3_h1)

question: What medical term is used to describe specific blind spots inside a person's field of vision?

options.A: Cataracts

question: What is a major neurological risk for someone with poorly managed high blood pressure?

options.A: Increased production of cerebrospinal fluid
options.B: Spinal cord nerve degeneration
options.C: Cerebrovascular accident or stroke
options.D: Permanent loss of sensory nerve conduction

explanation: Constant high pressure can weaken brain blood vessels until they burst or block off, causing a stroke (cerebrovascular accident). [learn more](GNS111_U2_T6#GNS111_U2_T6_h8)

question: What makes home health care nursing ethically different from hospital nursing?

options.A: The nurse works alone inside a private domestic environment
options.B: Patients at home have fewer legal rights than hospital patients
options.C: Hospital nurses do not need to follow ethical principles
options.D: Home care nurses are exempt from professional licensing boards

explanation: Spot on! Working inside a private home means you are stepping out of a structured hospital and into someone's personal space, which brings unique ethical situations. You've got this! [learn more](GNS324_U1_T10#GNS324_U1_T10_h1)

question: What complication can develop in a patient who suffers from severe, unmanaged fear throughout a long hospital stay?

options.A: Complete immunity to all future bacterial infections
options.B: Post-traumatic stress symptoms related to the medical experience
options.C: Instant recovery from chronic respiratory illnesses
options.D: Permanent loss of the sense of taste and smell

explanation: Well done! Extreme, unmanaged distress during medical care can unfortunately leave long-lasting psychological scars. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T11#GNS123_U3_T11_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of community sensitization?

options.A: To raise awareness and correct health misconceptions
options.B: To collect taxes from local market traders
options.C: To distribute free medical textbooks
options.D: To punish people who break sanitation laws

explanation: Sensitization aims to inform people about health risks and clear up wrong beliefs using culturally friendly communication methods. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h3)

question: What is the primary mechanism of an autoclave in waste treatment?

options.A: Dissolving metal instruments in strong acids
options.B: Burning waste at extremely high open flames

question: Even after physical withdrawal fades, why is quitting smoking still so tough?

question: Why are imaging studies like an MRI necessary after finding high hormone levels in the blood?

question: Which insect is the main carrier that spreads yellow fever in towns and cities?

question: Why do nurses love using line diagrams instead of long tables of numbers to track trends?

options.A: They completely eliminate the need to collect raw numerical data.

options.C: They prevent any mathematical errors from happening during data entry.
options.D: They make it much easier to spot upward or downward movement at a single glance.

question: What is the main goal of risk management in nursing?

options.A: Increasing the number of daily patient admissions
options.B: Protecting patients, staff, and facilities from harm
options.C: Punishing staff members who make clinical errors
options.D: Reducing the cost of hospital equipment purchases

question: How do cultural misconceptions about disabilities directly impact a special child?

options.A: They motivate rapid medical diagnosis in rural clinics
options.B: They improve community volunteer participation
options.C: They often lead families to hide the child away due to shame or fear
options.D: They guarantee immediate government scholarship awards

question: The neural tube, which forms the brain and spinal cord, develops from which germ layer?

question: What does the term 'groupnorms' mean in a nursing unit?

question: Which hormone triggers the release of stored energy when the body is fasting?

options.A: Insulin
options.B: Gastrin
options.C: Prolactin

question: Why is psychological first aid provided by nurses so important after a disaster?

options.A: It helps traumatized survivors cope with immediate shock, grief, and emotional distress
options.B: It immediately repairs damaged physical infrastructure like roads and houses
options.C: It cures chronic physical diseases that existed before the disaster
options.D: It replaces the need for surgical operations in severe trauma cases

question: Two senior nurses are arguing bitterly over shift schedules, and the manager encourages both to give up a preferred off-day to meet in the middle. Which style is this?

options.C: Compromise

question: What turns raw clinical numbers into useful clinical information?

options.C: Information places raw facts into a meaningful context
options.D: Information is gathered only by physicians during rounds

question: Why do healthcare teams hold professional meetings?

options.B: Evaluating individual nurses on daily bedside tasks
options.C: Replacing all written forms of hospital communication
options.D: Providing a space for extended social interactions

question: A patient is healing from surgery and needs to build new tissue. Which process is at work?

options.C: Osmosis, because it balances electrolytes in the blood
options.D: Catabolism, because it destroys old cells to provide water

question: A public health nurse distributes insecticide-treated nets to families in a rural malaria-endemic village. Which prevention strategy is this?

options.A: Primordial legislation
options.B: Specific protection
options.C: Tertiary rehabilitation
options.D: Secondary screening

question: Why must data collection instruments be valid and reliable in cross-sectional research?

options.A: To make sure patients take their medications on time
options.B: To guarantee that the study takes at least five years to finish
options.C: To prevent the researcher from having to use statistics
options.D: To ensure the measurements are accurate and consistent

question: What is a major challenge for tele-nursing in developing regions?

options.A: Unstable electricity and poor internet connectivity

options.C: Too many advanced devices confusing the patients
options.D: An excess of high-speed satellite networks

explanation: Spot on. Power outages and poor network signals can make remote monitoring tricky, which is a common hurdle we navigate. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h3)

question: What is the primary goal of public information during a disaster?

options.A: To generate revenue for local agencies
options.B: To save lives and reduce panic
options.C: To test new telecommunication networks
options.D: To document property damage for insurance

explanation: Clear information prevents chaos and helps people take quick safety measures to protect themselves. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T9#GNS315_U5_T9_h1)

question: Which nursing action shows the best way to assess a patient's emotional state during a crisis?

options.A: Observing for non-verbal cues like trembling and hypervigilance

options.C: Telling the patient to stop worrying because the danger has passed

explanation: Great clinical instinct! Watching for body language, like shaking or being overly jumpy, helps you safely understand how much distress your patient is holding inside. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T3#GNS314_U6_T3_h4)

question: Why do hospitals nowadays rarely give whole blood to patients?

options.A: Whole blood carries no oxygen-carrying capacity

options.D: Processing whole blood is too expensive for hospitals

question: According to safety science, what is usually at the root of most medical errors in hospitals?

options.A: They are completely unavoidable in modern hospitals.
options.B: They occur only in surgical departments.
options.C: They are caused entirely by careless staff members.
options.D: They usually stem from complex system failures.

question: A patient is officially diagnosed with AIDS when their CD4 count drops below which threshold?

options.A: 800 cells/mm3
options.B: 200 cells/mm3
options.C: 500 cells/mm3
options.D: 1000 cells/mm3

question: Which residential model features 24-hour staff presence for high support?

options.A: Self-contained private flats
options.B: Supervised hostels
options.C: Temporary weekend shelters
options.D: Transitional living facilities

question: What is a baby or young child's biggest emotional need?

options.A: Having their own money from an early age
options.B: Being left alone to learn how to be independent early
options.C: Advanced problem-solving skills for handling stress
options.D: Consistent love and predictable routines to build trust

question: How does the ICD stand apart from the DSM?

options.B: The ICD covers all general medical conditions, not just mental disorders
options.C: The ICD is published by a local psychiatric association
options.D: The ICD is only used for nursing documentation in emergency rooms

question: Why might a woman with an epidural during labor not realize her bladder is getting too full?

question: Why do intersectoral teams sometimes struggle to communicate with each other?

options.A: Nurses refuse to share office space with workers from other government departments
options.B: Government policies legally forbid workers from different ministries from talking
options.C: Different professional sectors use unique terminology and focus on different priorities

question: Why is a biopsy a must-have test when checking for cancer?

options.C: It completely cures the patient by removing all toxins.

question: What is the main legal fear many healthcare workers have about apologizing?

question: What is the medical term for when a child starts going through puberty much earlier than normal?

options.C: Acromegaly
options.D: Delayed puberty

question: What is the immediate priority when caring for a patient who has just suffered a severe burn injury?

options.A: Applying antibiotic ointment to all blistered areas

options.C: Inserting a large-bore intravenous line for pain meds
options.D: Securing the airway and assessing breathing

question: What is the main job of the chairperson during a professional meeting?

options.A: Serving refreshments to all invited attendees
options.B: Guiding discussion and keeping the team on the agenda
options.C: Taking over patient care duties while staff are away
options.D: Writing down every single word spoken by participants

explanation: The chairperson leads the session, manages time, and ensures the group sticks to the planned topics. [learn more](GST321_U7_T4#GST321_U7_T4_h4)

question: Which four elements form the main building blocks of most nutrients in our diet?

options.A: Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and nitrogen
options.B: Phosphorus, sulfur, chlorine, and magnesium
options.C: Calcium, iron, sodium, and potassium
options.D: Copper, zinc, iodine, and manganese

question: What must you often handle first before trying to teach a patient about their discharge medications?

options.A: Discharge paperwork completion
options.B: Full payment of hospital bills
options.C: Severe pain or acute distress
options.D: Complete recovery of normal gait

question: What is a primary responsibility of a nurse working in an assisted living facility?

options.A: Managing hospital emergency room admissions
options.B: Monitoring health status and coordinating care services
options.C: Running the facility financial and accounting department
options.D: Performing major surgical operations on-site

question: Why is it necessary to use redundant communication systems during a disaster response?

options.C: Different agencies are legally banned from using mobile phones
options.D: Standard cellular networks and internet lines frequently collapse

question: Why is spotting a high-risk labour early on so important for us as nurses?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for any postpartum medication
options.B: It allows the hospital to discharge the patient within one hour
options.C: It guarantees the mother will experience a painless delivery
options.D: It prevents small problems from turning into life-threatening emergencies

explanation: Spotting risks early is a superpower in nursing! It gives our team time to step in before a small issue turns into a major crisis. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T004#GNS226_U4_T004_h1)

question: What does an 'informed culture' depend on most in daily hospital work?

options.A: Strict rules that penalize any minor deviation
options.B: Leaving safety decisions entirely to hospital directors
options.C: Ignoring small mistakes that do not harm patients
options.D: An understanding of factors affecting safe patient care

explanation: Think of it as staying aware! An informed culture keeps all staff mindful of the everyday things—like fatigue or busy shifts—that can impact how safely we care for patients. [learn more](GST319_U6_T6#GST319_U6_T6_h2)

question: Why are clinical supervision and peer support so important for nurses working in crisis settings?

options.A: They ensure that nurses never feel empathy for their patients
options.B: They are used primarily to penalize nurses who make charting errors
options.C: They help prevent burnout and address secondary trauma from exposure to crisis stories
options.D: They replace the need for formal psychiatric nursing education

question: What is a 'status offense'?

options.B: Any offense that results in immediate capital punishment
options.C: A minor traffic violation committed by a licensed driver
options.D: A violent crime committed by an adult against a child

explanation: You're doing great! A status offense is an action that is only breaking the rule because of the offender's young age—like skipping school or running away from home. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T4#GNS225_U5_T4_h3)

question: Why is standardization especially critical for plant-derived medicines?

options.A: Natural herbs are completely unregulated by international health bodies.
options.B: Plants always contain dangerous levels of synthetic chemical additives.
options.C: Soil and climate variations can change the concentration of active ingredients in plants.
options.D: Plant-derived medications never dissolve properly in human digestive fluids.

explanation: Weather and soil changes mean plants can have different strengths of active ingredients. Standardization ensures every tablet has the exact right dose! [learn more](GNS125_U2_T3#GNS125_U2_T3_h6)

question: What does a high-pressure alarm on a mechanical ventilator usually mean?

options.A: The breathing tube has fallen out entirely
options.B: The patient's body temperature has suddenly dropped
options.C: There is a blockage or kink in the airway tubing
options.D: The hospital oxygen tank is completely empty

explanation: High-pressure alarms sound when the ventilator hits resistance trying to push air in—often due to secretions, a mucus plug, or the patient biting the tube. Spot on! [learn more](GNS315_U4_T2#GNS315_U4_T2_h5)

question: Which two techniques form the core of a routine musculoskeletal physical examination?

options.A: Inspection and palpation
options.B: Palpation and percussion
options.C: Inspection and auscultation
options.D: Percussion and auscultation

explanation: While all four physical assessment techniques have a place, looking closely at structure and feeling for tenderness or swelling are used most constantly in bone and muscle checks. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T3#GNS222_U1_T3_h1)

question: What does a valid research instrument do?

options.D: Gives the exact same results every time

explanation: Validity is all about accuracy, meaning the tool actually captures the specific concept being studied. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T21#GNS224_U1_T21_h2)

question: How do most harmful bacteria in food usually get passed around?

options.C: From mosquito bites near kitchen drains
options.D: Through the fecal-oral route via dirty hands, water, or food

question: What is the main goal of workplace ergonomics in nursing?

options.A: Reducing the number of patients assigned to each nurse
options.B: Eliminating the need for taking breaks during a shift
options.C: Fitting the work environment and equipment to the worker
options.D: Speeding up the documentation process on computer terminals

explanation: Spot on! Ergonomics is all about shaping your tools and workspace to match your body, making your daily tasks safer and more comfortable. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h1)

question: Which body is responsible for regulating nursing practice and setting professional standards in Nigeria?

question: Why is proper waste disposal so important right from the start in a field hospital?

options.C: To prevent secondary disease outbreaks in the camp

question: What is a key nursing check before giving medication to a pregnant patient?

options.D: Prescribe an alternative drug with fewer side effects

question: A Nigerian dietitian is counseling a patient with high blood pressure who has a modest income. What is the most practical advice?

options.C: Advise the patient to stop eating all local carbohydrates completely
options.D: Prescribe expensive imported supplements available only online

question: Which sector is primarily responsible for crowd control and maintaining safety during a disaster?

question: What is the significance of menarche (a girl's first period) during pubertal development?

question: Which group is generally at the highest risk of abuse and neglect in home care settings?

question: What technology does an autoclave use to make infectious medical waste safe?

question: Why do healthcare workers sometimes feel resistant when a brand new clinical protocol is introduced?

question: What does a line that slopes upward on a healthcare chart tell you?

question: Why is post-abortion care viewed as a complete package rather than just a single medical procedure?

question: Why do nurses make mitered corners when tucking in hospital bed sheets?

question: During which gestational weeks is screening for gestational diabetes routinely performed in uncomplicated pregnancies?

question: Why do we take off our gloves FIRST before removing other PPE items?

question: What is the main job of Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH) when your body needs to hold onto water?

question: Which of the following is a common barrier to effective family planning referrals in Nigeria?

question: Which of these commonly used IV fluids is classified as an isotonic fluid?

question: What is an example of community mobilization in primary health care?

question: In the famous Swiss Cheese Model, what do the holes in the cheese slices represent?

question: If a fuel tanker explodes in a busy local market, which teams need to rush to the scene right away?

question: What is the main goal of monitoring a patient after giving them a medication?

question: What does 'psychological safety' mean for a clinical healthcare team?

question: What does the nursing abbreviation MSE stand for?

options.D: Mood State Estimator

question: What is a major financial benefit of healthcare sectors sharing their resources?

question: Why do nurse-midwives treat every pregnancy as a condition that needs careful monitoring?

question: What does mutual respect mean within a healthcare team?

question: What is the primary role of nurses regarding disability policy frameworks?

question: A patient getting a fast IV infusion of vancomycin suddenly has a red face and neck. What's going on?

question: Which of the following is an example of objective, professional documentation for a wound dressing change?

question: When is it legally and ethically okay to use physical restraints or seclusion on a ward?

question: In an emergency, when would a nurse use a defibrillator?

question: How did home health nursing get its start way back when?

question: What security practice involves giving staff access only to the patient files needed for their specific job duties?

question: A researcher wants to show how blood pressure readings changed across four different clinic visits for a group of patients. Which format should they choose?

question: What is the main food and energy source that fuels a growing fetus?

question: You receive your handoff report and hear about four different tasks. Which one needs your immediate action?

question: What is a common socioeconomic barrier to good nutrition?

question: What is the nurse's main role when a patient wants to use alternative therapies?

question: What is the main job of the Leydig cells found in the testes?

question: A nurse wants to chat with a patient across a state border using a regular social media app. What is the main risk here?

question: Why should you sort waste right at the bedside or where it is generated?

question: How is Psychological First Aid (PFA) different from formal psychotherapy?

question: Why should nurses avoid using heavy medical jargon when teaching community members?

options.B: Transcription error
options.C: Duplicate entry
options.D: Wrong-patient charting

question: Which conflict management strategy involves both sides working together to find a solution that satisfies everyone?

options.A: Collaboration
options.B: Accommodation
options.C: Avoidance
options.D: Domination

explanation: Collaboration focuses on open dialogue and problem-solving to achieve a win-win outcome for all involved parties. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T13#GNS124_U5_T13_h5)

question: What is the main fertility option for a patient who has no fallopian tubes at all?

options.A: Tubal reanastomosis surgery
options.B: In vitro fertilization (IVF)
options.C: Endometrial ablation therapy
options.D: Ovarian hormone stimulation alone

explanation: Spot on! Since IVF places a fertilized egg directly into the uterus, it completely bypasses the need for fallopian tubes. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T28#GNS216_U5_T28_h6)

question: Which action directly helps keep nurses on the job by letting them have a say in their workplace?

options.A: Involving frontline staff in scheduling committees
options.B: Eliminating all mentorship and peer support programs
options.C: Increasing the number of mandatory night shifts
options.D: Relying entirely on remote electronic surveillance

explanation: When nurses help make decisions that affect their daily lives—like putting together duty rosters—they feel respected and stay longer! [learn more](GST321_U3_T6#GST321_U3_T6_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical feature of untreated or severe endometritis?

options.A: Normal spontaneous resolution without any treatment
options.B: Spread of infection into the bloodstream
options.C: Scarring of the inner uterine cavity
options.D: Formation of pus pockets in the pelvis

explanation: Endometritis is serious and won't just go away on its own. Leaving it untreated can lead to nasty complications like abscesses or blood infections. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T20#GNS216_U5_T20_h8)

question: Which checklist type is best for checking if specific steps are done in the right order?

options.A: Task or process checklist
options.B: Unstructured narrative log
options.C: Biographical data form
options.D: Patient satisfaction survey

explanation: A process checklist breaks down a procedure step-by-step so you can tick them off as they happen in real-time. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T23#GNS224_U1_T23_h3)

question: Which of these is an example of a strong system-level fix to prevent errors?

options.A: Redesigning automated medication dispensing cabinets to require double scans
options.B: Warning staff that future mistakes will result in immediate termination
options.C: Removing all safety policies to let nurses rely entirely on instinct
options.D: Telling nurses to pay closer attention so they never get tired

explanation: Brilliant! Changing technology and workflows creates a strong safety net that protects against human error much better than just telling staff to be careful. [learn more](GST319_U6_T2#GST319_U6_T2_h7)

question: Which group of symptoms strongly points towards preeclampsia in a pregnant patient?

options.A: Low blood pressure, excessive sleepiness, and hunger
options.B: Frequent urination, mild thirst, and dry skin
options.C: High blood pressure, headache, and visual disturbances
options.D: Lower back pain and increased appetite

explanation: You nailed it! Preeclampsia is marked by high blood pressure paired with stubborn headaches and blurry vision. Always watch out for this! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T009#GNS226_U2_T009_h6)

question: Why is it so tricky to make drugs that kill parasites without harming human patients?

options.A: Parasites share a similar eukaryotic cell structure with human hosts
options.B: Human immune systems cannot produce antibodies against parasites
options.C: Parasites replicate much faster than bacterial pathogens
options.D: Antiparasitic medications are always destroyed by stomach acid

explanation: You've got this! Because both human cells and parasites are eukaryotic (complex cells with a nucleus), it's tough to design a medicine that attacks the parasite without hurting our own cells. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T1#GNS215_U6_T1_h1)

question: How do thorough tracking records help healthcare facility managers over time?

options.A: They allow the hospital to fine clients who miss clinic days
options.B: They highlight recurring community barriers and help improve service delivery
options.C: They ensure that nurses never have to talk to clients directly
options.D: They eliminate all paperwork from the nursing station

explanation: When we track patterns, managers can spot common roadblocks—like transport challenges or drug stockouts—and fix them for everyone! [learn more](GNS226_U6_T025#GNS226_U6_T025_h7)

question: What is the big advantage of using a moist cold compress instead of a stiff ice pack?

options.A: They require no refrigeration or ice whatsoever
options.B: They completely eliminate the risk of frostbite
options.C: They mold easily to uneven body contours like the jaw or face
options.D: They stay warm for up to twelve hours at a time

explanation: You got it! Faces and jaws aren't flat, so a flexible moist compress hugs those tricky curves much better than a rigid ice pack. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T8#GNS221_U3_T8_h4)

question: Why do youth health programmes include counseling against substance abuse?

options.A: Substance use is a legal matter handled exclusively by police officers.
options.B: Alcohol and drugs are only used by teenagers.
options.C: Lifestyle habits formed during youth heavily influence long-term health outcomes.
options.D: It is a requirement to receive government funding for equipment.

explanation: Spot on! Habits picked up in the teenage years often stick around. Catching substance use early helps prevent lifelong health struggles. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T48#GNS214_U1_T48_h4)

question: Why is it so important to tape and secure the NG tube firmly to the patient's nose?

options.A: To stop the stomach from producing normal digestive acids
options.B: To prevent friction and trauma to the nasal mucosa from tube movement
options.C: To make the tube completely invisible from the outside
options.D: To ensure the patient can easily remove the tube themselves

explanation: If the tube slides around, it rubs against delicate nose tissue and causes painful sores. Securing it well keeps your patient comfortable. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T1#GNS212_U1_T1_h6)

question: What should you do immediately if a patient shows signs of pain while their arm is being moved?

options.A: Continue moving faster to get past the painful spot
options.B: Ask a relative to hold the arm down so you can finish
options.C: Stop the exercise right away and check the joint
options.D: Ignore it because passive exercise always hurts

explanation: Pain is your stop sign! It tells you something is being over-stretched or injured. Always pause and assess. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h4)

question: What is a common dietary consequence for workers holding multiple exhausting jobs?

options.A: Strict adherence to fresh, raw vegetable diets
options.B: Heavy reliance on fast food and convenient ready-made meals
options.C: Increased consumption of home-cooked traditional breakfasts
options.D: Complete elimination of snacking between work shifts

explanation: Exhaustion and lack of time push overworked individuals toward quick, convenient food options that require no preparation. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T020#GNS227_U2_T020_h6)

question: What communication habit should a nurse avoid when explaining a new medication to a patient?

options.A: Using heavy medical jargon that the patient cannot easily follow
options.B: Encouraging the patient to speak up if they have any worries
options.C: Slowing down the conversation to match the client's pace
options.D: Asking open-ended questions about how they plan to take the pills

explanation: Complex medical terminology confuses patients and prevents them from truly understanding their treatment plan. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T3#GNS125_U3_T3_h5)

question: What is the main duty of NAFDAC regarding medications?

options.A: Providing free meals to hospitalized patients
options.B: Regulating drug manufacturing, importation, and quality
options.C: Issuing practicing licenses to individual bedside nurses
options.D: Managing the internal budget of teaching hospitals

explanation: NAFDAC ensures that all drugs sold or used in the country are safe, effective, and of good quality. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T13#GNS122_U1_T13_h3)

question: What does the 'halo effect' mean during a staff performance evaluation?

options.A: The hospital evaluates staff based solely on patient mortality rates
options.B: A nurse refuses to accept constructive criticism from the supervisor
options.C: An employee receives a bonus for working night shifts during holidays
options.D: A manager lets one good trait unfairly influence the whole review

explanation: Just like a halo makes someone look like an angel, the halo effect happens when a manager is so impressed by one good quality (like punctuality) that they ignore areas where the nurse actually needs improvement. [learn more](GST321_U4_T1#GST321_U4_T1_h5)

question: Cell-mediated immunity is best at handling which type of problem?

options.A: Dissolved chemical toxins in body fluids
options.B: Free-floating bacteria in blood plasma
options.C: Large parasites floating in the gut lumen
options.D: Viruses hiding inside host cells

explanation: When viruses sneak and hide inside your own body cells, antibodies alone can't reach them. That's when cell-mediated immunity (using T cells) steps in to hunt them down! [learn more](GST114_U4_T6#GST114_U4_T6_h6)

question: Which infection control step is absolutely mandatory when nursing a suspected Lassa fever patient?

options.A: Placing every patient in a carpeted, air-conditioned room
options.B: Allowing family members to wash the patient's soiled linens
options.C: Using full personal protective equipment and barrier nursing
options.D: Administering prophylactic antibiotics to all hospital visitors

explanation: Barrier nursing with full PPE is non-negotiable to keep infectious body fluids away from staff and other patients. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T8#GNS214_U1_T8_h8)

question: Why is the structure of the urethra different in males compared to females?

options.A: The female bladder sits at a much lower angle in the pelvic cavity
options.B: Male urine contains thicker waste products that require a wider path
options.C: It must accommodate the male reproductive organs and dual functions
options.D: Females require a longer tube to prevent frequent bladder infections

explanation: Great thinking! In men, the urethra has to travel through the prostate and penis, serving both the urinary and reproductive systems. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T4#GNS121_U2_T4_h1)

question: A patient has a severe spinal cord injury needing advanced surgery. Where should they be sent?

options.A: Outpatient clinic
options.B: Community post
options.C: Tertiary level
options.D: Primary level

explanation: Spot on! Complex cases like major spine injuries need specialized tertiary hospitals with advanced equipment and expert surgical teams. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T5#GNS225_U2_T5_h3)

question: Which of these is a major home hazard that can cause older adults to fall?

options.A: Having too many windows in the bedroom
options.B: Loose carpets and inadequate lighting
options.C: Using electric fans during warm weather
options.D: Brightly painted walls in the hallway

explanation: Simple things like dim hallways or loose rugs are major tripping hazards. Home safety assessments are a key part of community nursing care for the elderly! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T2#GNS324_U3_T2_h4)

question: Why is it risky to think of urine leaking as just a normal part of getting older?

options.A: It causes severe skin rashes in all elderly people
options.B: It stops patients from seeking helpful treatment
options.C: It automatically leads to kidney failure
options.D: It means the bladder has completely stopped working

explanation: When patients or their families think leaking is just normal aging, they keep quiet and miss out on treatments that could really help them feel better. Great insight for a nurse! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T17#GNS212_U1_T17_h1)

question: How do intestinal parasite eggs most commonly spread to people?

options.A: Mosquito vector bites
options.B: The fecal-oral route
options.C: Direct airborne droplets
options.D: Unprotected skin contact

explanation: Most gut parasites spread when tiny amounts of contaminated matter reach the mouth via unwashed hands, food, or water. Good to know for patient education! [learn more](GST114_U3_T8#GST114_U3_T8_h4)

question: What part do environmental factors play in kicking off an autoimmune disease?

options.A: They directly replace damaged genes in the bone marrow
options.B: They cure chronic inflammation by boosting white blood cells
options.C: They prevent the formation of autoantibodies
options.D: They can act as triggers that awaken an underlying immune vulnerability

explanation: Think of genetics as the loaded gun, and environmental triggers—like a nasty infection or stress—as the finger pulling the trigger. [learn more](GST114_U4_T8#GST114_U4_T8_h3)

question: Why is routine immunization considered a vital part of Primary Health Care?

options.A: It serves as a primary surgical cure for congenital heart defects
options.B: It is used exclusively to treat chronic lifestyle diseases in adults
options.C: It replaces the need for proper nutrition and clean drinking water
options.D: It actively prevents children from contracting dangerous, vaccine-preventable infectious diseases

explanation: Immunization is a powerful shield that stops deadly childhood infections before they can spread. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h4)

question: What emotional need is especially important for elderly family members?

options.A: Trying to fit in with teenage trends
options.B: Feeling respected and protected from loneliness
options.C: Wanting zero help from anyone at all
options.D: Living in high-stress, competitive environments

explanation: As people age and face physical changes, knowing they are valued, respected, and not forgotten keeps their spirits high and emotional health intact. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T6#GNS314_U1_T6_h3)

question: Why shouldn't a nurse just do everything for a slow patient who can manage with a tool?

options.A: To save nursing time for charting and other patients
options.B: To ensure the patient finishes dressing before visiting hours
options.C: To foster independence and prevent learned helplessness
options.D: Because hospital policy strictly forbids nurse assistance

explanation: Brilliant! We want to cheer them on to do it themselves so they don't become overly dependent on us. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T5#GNS123_U6_T5_h5)

question: Why can checking a patient's blood composition tell us so much about their overall health?

options.A: Blood circulates through every organ system and directly reflects whole-body health
options.B: Blood pressure remains completely constant regardless of any underlying organ damage
options.C: Blood cells are the largest cells in the human body and easily visible under basic light
options.D: Blood is the only fluid in the body that contains water and dissolved electrolytes

explanation: Spot on! Because blood travels everywhere, it picks up waste and drops off nutrients in every organ. Looking at blood work is like checking the report card for the entire body. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T1#GNS111_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why are babies and young children extra vulnerable to the risks of self-medication?

options.A: They refuse to swallow any medication unless it is sweet
options.B: Their liver and kidney enzyme systems are still immature
options.C: Their skin absorbs chemical substances much slower than adults
options.D: They have higher blood volume than healthy adults

explanation: Spot on! Children's bodies process drugs differently because their organs aren't fully developed yet to clear toxins easily. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T4#GNS215_U4_T4_h7)

question: During family planning, a client is hesitant about a method because of what their mother-in-law said. What should you do?

options.A: Choose a method for the client to save time and avoid family conflict
options.B: Support the client's personal preferences and explore their individual needs
options.C: Tell the client to ignore all family advice completely
options.D: Insist that the mother-in-law be brought into the room to decide

explanation: Great choice! We must always protect our patient's autonomy and help them choose what fits their personal health goals. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T6#GNS312_U4_T6_h5)

question: A rural clinic nurse finds that many women prefer giving birth at home. What is the best first step for the nurse?

options.A: Engage community leaders and educate women on the safety of facility delivery
options.B: Report all pregnant women who plan home births to the local police
options.C: Close the clinic until the women agree to come in voluntarily
options.D: Ignore the practice since home delivery has no real risks

explanation: Working hand-in-hand with village leaders builds trust and helps women see the safety and benefits of delivering at a health facility. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h8)

question: Which activity is an example of non-structural disaster mitigation?

options.A: Installing steel reinforcement pillars in a hospital ward
options.B: Purchasing heavy-duty earthquake-resistant generators
options.C: Building a high concrete wall around a reservoir
options.D: Enforcing strict zoning laws to stop building in floodplains

explanation: That's right! Laws and policies are non-structural measures that guide us away from dangerous areas without physical building changes. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T11#GNS315_U5_T11_h4)

question: Why is keeping things confidential so vital when caring for teenagers?

options.A: It stops teenagers from needing any physical examinations at all
options.B: It guarantees that the adolescent will never experience an infection
options.C: It encourages teenagers to truthfully disclose sensitive health and lifestyle information
options.D: It is a legal requirement that prevents parents from ever knowing their child is sick

explanation: Teens worry about being judged. When we promise confidentiality, we build the trust they need to open up and tell us the truth about their health. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T1#GNS312_U3_T1_h6)

question: Why do disaster coordinators try to house elderly or chronically ill patients close to the main medical tents?

options.A: To isolate them completely from the rest of the community
options.B: To allow for quicker response if their health condition suddenly deteriorates
options.C: To make it easier for them to clean the medical equipment
options.D: To reduce the walking distance for medical staff delivering food

explanation: Vulnerable patients can crash quickly in emergencies. Keeping them close to medical help means doctors and nurses can reach them in seconds. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T5#GNS315_U5_T5_h8)

question: Which blood test is the most reliable sign that heart muscle cells have been damaged?

options.A: Troponin
options.B: Complete blood count
options.C: Blood urea nitrogen
options.D: Serum electrolytes

explanation: That's right! Troponin is a special cardiac protein that spills into the bloodstream specifically when heart muscle cells get injured or start dying. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T10#GNS111_U2_T10_h5)

question: Which specific immune cells does HIV attack and destroy?

options.A: Red blood cells
options.B: Platelets
options.C: Neutrophils
options.D: CD4+ T helper cells

explanation: HIV targets CD4+ T helper cells, weakening the body's immune defenses over time. You've got this! [learn more](GNS216_U6_T13#GNS216_U6_T13_h1)

question: What is a simple, practical way to store extra green vegetables when electricity is unreliable?

options.A: Sealing in airtight glass jars with heavy salt
options.B: Soaking them continuously in vinegar
options.C: Sun-drying or blanching
options.D: Deep-freezing for three years

explanation: Correct! Sun-drying and blanching are time-tested ways to keep your veggies from spoiling without needing a fridge. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T009#GNS227_U4_T009_h6)

question: What does the term 'bioavailability' mean in nutrition?

options.A: The proportion of a nutrient successfully absorbed and used by the body
options.B: The total percentage of water contained within a specific food item
options.C: The total number of calories released when a food is burned
options.D: The speed at which food travels from the mouth to the stomach

explanation: Correct! Bioavailability just asks: out of all the nutrients you swallowed, how much actually made it into your bloodstream to do work? [learn more](GNS227_U1_T013#GNS227_U1_T013_h6)

question: Which of these is a major barrier to healthcare access in rural Nigerian communities?

options.A: Severe shortage of health facilities and poor road networks
options.B: Instant availability of advanced surgical equipment
options.C: Too many well-trained medical doctors per capita
options.D: Excessive number of specialized tertiary hospitals

explanation: Correct! Bad roads and faraway clinics make getting to a hospital a massive challenge for rural villagers. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h7)

question: What is a key feature of algorithmic standing orders?

options.A: They apply only to surgical procedures performed in tertiary hospitals
options.B: They require the nurse to call a doctor before every single step
options.C: They contain blank spaces for the nurse to write their own drug dosages
options.D: They use decision trees with branching questions to guide clinical choices

explanation: Algorithmic standing orders guide the clinician through a series of sequential questions based on patient findings to arrive at the correct care plan. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T6#GNS124_U6_T6_h3)

question: What is the primary focus of qualitative research methods?

options.A: Calculating patient weights on a digital scale
options.B: Exploring human experiences and meanings in depth
options.C: Measuring precise chemical levels in the blood
options.D: Counting the exact number of pills in a bottle

explanation: That's right! Qualitative research helps us understand people's feelings, stories, and subjective experiences. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T20#GNS224_U1_T20_h4)

question: What is a common myth about medication administration errors?

options.A: They only occur in busy surgical operating rooms
options.B: They are always the sole fault of the nurse at the bedside
options.C: They never result in any negative physical outcomes
options.D: They are completely eliminated by electronic health records

explanation: Even though the nurse gives the drug, the root cause might actually go back to prescribing, pharmacy dispensing, or unclear packaging! [learn more](GST319_U5_T5#GST319_U5_T5_h5)

question: Why should nurses worry when a patient has severe, ongoing itching?

options.A: It proves that the topical medication is working effectively
options.B: It always indicates that a patient has systemic kidney failure
options.C: Scratching breaks the skin barrier and increases infection risk
options.D: It prevents the formation of primary lesions like macules

explanation: The itch-scratch cycle damages the skin's natural defense shield, making it super easy for germs and bacteria to get in. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T8#GNS213_U5_T8_h5)

question: What is one of the primary roles of a psychiatric nurse working in community health?

options.A: Enforcing legal penalties for individuals who refuse counseling
options.B: Managing the financial accounts of local government clinics
options.C: Manufacturing pharmaceutical medications for local distribution
options.D: Acting as a bridge between clinical medicine and community life

explanation: Community psychiatric nurses connect clinical health services with the everyday realities and needs of the population. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T7#GNS314_U1_T7_h7)

question: A patient with tummy cramps needs an anti-spasmodic, but complains that dry mouth makes it hard to talk. What class of drug should you expect the doctor to switch them to?

options.A: High-dose anticholinergic agents
options.B: Parasympathetic nervous stimulants
options.C: Direct-acting smooth muscle relaxants
options.D: Strong bowel-motility accelerators

explanation: Spot on! Switching to a direct-acting relaxant helps the patient avoid those annoying drying side effects. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T4#GNS223_U3_T4_h4)

question: What is the primary significance of traditional West African medicine in modern pharmacology?

options.A: It focuses solely on spiritual healing without any physical remedies.
options.B: Modern researchers isolate active chemical compounds from plants used by indigenous healers.
options.C: It provides cheap synthetic drugs for rural Nigerian clinics.
options.D: It has completely replaced the need for synthetic antibiotics in hospitals.

explanation: Many modern drugs are developed by studying the plants that traditional healers have successfully used for centuries to treat common ailments. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T1#GNS125_U1_T1_h2)

question: What happens to the body during a state of positive energy balance?

options.A: It maintains a completely stable body weight
options.B: It burns stored fat to make up for a calorie deficit
options.C: It stores extra calories and gains weight
options.D: It stops all metabolic processes to save energy

explanation: When you take in more calories than you burn, the extra energy gets stored, primarily as fat, leading to weight gain. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h6)

question: What is the primary job of the protein dystrophin in healthy skeletal muscle?

options.A: Transporting calcium ions out of the sarcoplasmic reticulum
options.B: Generating the electrical action potential along the sarcolemma
options.C: Linking the muscle cell cytoskeleton to the extracellular matrix
options.D: Acting as the primary enzyme that breaks down glucose for energy

explanation: Dystrophin acts like a sturdy internal anchor, connecting the muscle cell's inner framework to its outer environment for stability during contractions. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T8#GNS121_U3_T8_h6)

question: What is a vital nursing duty once a patient is physically stable after an intentional overdose?

options.A: Scolding the patient to prevent them from trying it again
options.B: Restricting all family members from visiting the bedside
options.C: Discharging the patient immediately without further delay
options.D: Arranging a psychiatric evaluation and providing a safe space

explanation: Holistic nursing means caring for the mind too! Intentional overdoses call for compassionate mental health support and a safe, non-judgmental environment. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T9#GNS125_U2_T9_h7)

question: Which healthcare professional do home care nurses often team up with to improve patient mobility?

options.A: Hospital security guards
options.B: Pharmaceutical researchers
options.C: Financial accountants
options.D: Physical therapists

explanation: Physical therapists are fantastic partners! They work alongside nurses to help patients build strength, balance, and safely move around at home. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T9#GNS324_U3_T9_h8)

question: Why is active psychosis or severe mania a reason to hold off on granting leave?

options.A: Hospital rules strictly forbid patients with mood disorders from leaving
options.B: Family members never want to visit patients with mood disorders
options.C: Insurance companies refuse to pay for medications during outings
options.D: The patient lacks the stability and impulse control needed to stay safe in the community

explanation: When symptoms are still acute and uncontrolled, being outside a secure hospital can put the patient or others at risk. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h4)

question: What is an early and reliable warning sign that a patient is bleeding after having their tonsils out?

options.A: Complaints of a mild sore throat
options.B: Clear nasal discharge
options.C: Low-grade afternoon fever
options.D: Frequent swallowing

explanation: Correct! If a patient keeps swallowing over and over, it usually means fresh blood is trickling down the back of their throat from the surgical site. Always check this! [learn more](GNS311_U3_T5#GNS311_U3_T5_h6)

question: Why is recording the exact date and vaccine type so important for community health?

options.A: It proves to patients that the nurse has good handwriting
options.B: It allows the clinic to calculate daily financial profits
options.C: It prevents missed appointments and avoids duplicate dosing
options.D: It stops vaccine manufacturers from making more doses

explanation: Good records help us track when the next dose is due and make sure patients don't get accidental double doses. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T73#GNS214_U1_T73_h9)

question: What is the best first step for a nurse assessing a suspected victim of forced marriage?

options.A: Conduct a private interview away from family members or husbands
options.B: Call the local police department immediately while the patient is present
options.C: Ask the husband to explain why his young wife looks distressed
options.D: Discharge the patient with a pamphlet on community legal aid

explanation: Brilliant clinical instinct! Private time is a must because abusers or family members often watch over what the patient says. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T13#GNS312_U1_T13_h6)

question: During an exam, why do clinicians sometimes add potassium hydroxide (KOH) to a vaginal discharge sample?

options.A: To release a fishy odor in bacterial vaginosis
options.B: To lower the sample pH to an acidic level
options.C: To freeze the sample for laboratory transport
options.D: To stain the lactobacilli bacteria bright blue

explanation: It's called the 'whiff test'! Potassium hydroxide helps release those hidden smelly amines, making a fishy odor much easier to spot if BV is present. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T10#GNS216_U5_T10_h5)

question: Which of these is a clear example of primary cancer prevention?

options.A: Starting chemotherapy for a diagnosed breast lump
options.B: Undergoing a routine screening colonoscopy
options.C: Receiving the Hepatitis B vaccine
options.D: Performing a monthly self-breast examination

explanation: Brilliant! Primary prevention stops a disease before it even starts. Giving vaccines against cancer-linked viruses like Hepatitis B is a classic way to protect the body early. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T3#GNS321_U1_T3_h2)

question: Which medication is the standard, go-to antidote for a paracetamol (acetaminophen) overdose?

options.A: Atropine
options.B: Flumazenil
options.C: Naloxone
options.D: Acetylcysteine

explanation: You'll see this often in practice! Acetylcysteine saves the liver by restocking glutathione, which neutralizes the toxic breakdown products of paracetamol. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T3#GNS215_U5_T3_h7)

question: A community health nurse sets up a free blood sugar screening in the market. What level of prevention is this?

options.A: Tertiary prevention
options.B: Secondary prevention
options.C: Primary prevention
options.D: Universal prevention

question: Why is fighting social stigma just as important as giving medicine when dealing with airborne diseases?

options.A: Social isolation changes the physical structure of droplet nuclei
options.B: Community rumors replace the need for diagnostic laboratory tests
options.C: Fear of discrimination often causes patients to delay seeking care
options.D: Stigma directly inactivates the bacteria inside the lungs

explanation: So true! When people are afraid of being judged or stigmatized, they hide their sickness and stay away from clinics, which unfortunately lets the disease spread further. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T96#GNS214_U1_T96_h7)

question: A patient has a roundworm infection. Which family of worms is responsible?

options.A: Trematodes
options.B: Nematodes
options.C: Cestodes
options.D: Bacteriodes

explanation: Well done! Roundworms belong to the nematode family, known for their smooth, cylindrical, unsegmented bodies. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T7#GNS223_U3_T7_h2)

question: How do isolation methods mainly stop infections from spreading?

options.A: By destroying the causative agent inside the body
options.B: By blocking the mode of transmission
options.C: By eliminating all reservoirs on the hospital ward
options.D: By making the host completely immune to disease

explanation: By putting up physical barriers like gloves, masks, and private rooms, we cut off the path germs use to travel to new hosts. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h2)

question: What is the purpose of using Boolean operators like AND in a literature search?

options.A: To automatically translate foreign medical terms into English
options.B: To print research articles directly to the nurse station
options.C: To combine keywords and narrow down search results
options.D: To check if a website is legally safe to browse

explanation: Boolean operators help structure search queries so you retrieve articles specifically relevant to your exact clinical question. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h3)

question: What is a key responsibility of the psychiatric nurse in continuing care?

options.A: Managing hospital finances and staff payroll budgets
options.B: Observing mental status and evaluating medication side effects
options.C: Prescribing brand new antipsychotic drugs independently
options.D: Diagnosing rare surgical disorders in the community

question: What is the main focus of primary healthcare?

options.A: Delivering emergency critical care in intensive care units
options.B: Providing first-contact preventive care and treating common illnesses
options.C: Managing severe long-term illnesses in specialized facilities
options.D: Performing complex open-heart surgeries and organ transplants

explanation: You've got this! Primary care is simply the first door patients open in the health system. It's all about stopping sickness before it starts and treating everyday health issues. [learn more](GST322_U4_T11#GST322_U4_T11_h1)

question: As a working nurse, why is it helpful to understand basic data processing?

options.B: To replace hospital statisticians during busy morning shifts
options.C: To manage the hospital financial payroll system directly
options.D: To diagnose rare diseases without using laboratory tests

question: How does a joint venture differ from standard facility outsourcing?

options.A: It relies entirely on public funding while private staff do all the work

options.C: It prohibits any form of clinical service delivery within the partnership

question: How does carrying excess body weight contribute directly to knee osteoarthritis?

options.C: It causes the leg muscles to weaken and shrink away completely

question: What is the main purpose of multi-sectorial collaboration during a disaster?

options.A: To allow different agencies to work as a unified front

options.C: To reduce the total number of volunteers needed
options.D: To ensure only government agencies handle relief funds

question: Where should a nurse refer a client who requests a permanent surgical contraceptive method like bilateral tubal ligation?
